ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: When an unsymmetrical alkene such as propene is treated with N-bromosuccinimide in aqueous dimethyl sulfoxide, the major product has the bromine atom bonded to the less highly substituted carbon atom. Is this a Markovnikov or non-Markovnikov orientation?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: When an unsymmetrical alkene such as propene is treated with N-bromosuccinimide in aqueous dimethyl sulfoxide, the major product has the bromine atom bonded to the less highly substituted carbon atom. Is this a Markovnikov or non-Markovnikov orientation?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, the reactant is propene, written as CH3CH=CH2; above the arrow is labeled Br2, H2O; the product is a bromohydrin, with structure CH3CH(OH)CH2Br, that is, OH is attached to the middle, more substituted carbon, and Br is attached to the terminal CH2, the less substituted carbon. Reasoning: The problem conditions state N-bromosuccinimide in aqueous dimethyl sulfoxide, and state that in the major product the bromine atom is bonded to the less substituted carbon. For a halohydrin formation reaction, when judging Markovnikov/non-Markovnikov, look at the overall addition orientation: a halohydrin product in which OH adds to the more substituted carbon and halogen adds to the less substituted carbon is conventionally classified as Markovnikov orientation. Therefore, this orientation is Markovnikov orientation.

raw_record.question_text: When an unsymmetrical alkene such as propene is treated with N-bromosuccinimide in aqueous dimethyl sulfoxide, the major product has the bromine atom bonded to the less highly substituted carbon atom. Is this a Markovnikov or non-Markovnikov orientation?

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the alkene is propene and the product shown is a bromohydrin with OH on the middle carbon and Br on the terminal CH2 carbon. From the text, confirm the condition is NBS/aqueous DMSO and that bromine is bonded to the less highly substituted carbon. Apply the halohydrin regiochemistry convention: because the OH group is placed on the more substituted carbon, this is classified as Markovnikov orientation, even though Br is on the less substituted carbon.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：附图中反应物是丙烯，写作 CH3CH=CH2；箭头上方标有 Br2, H2O；产物是溴醇，结构为 CH3CH(OH)CH2Br，即 OH 连在中间的较高取代碳上，Br 连在末端 CH2 的较低取代碳上。推理：题干条件写的是 N-溴代琥珀酰亚胺在含水二甲基亚砜中，且说明主要产物中溴原子键合到较少取代的碳。对于卤醇形成反应，判断 Markovnikov/非 Markovnikov 时看整体加成取向：OH 加到较多取代碳、卤素加到较少取代碳的卤醇产物按惯例归为 Markovnikov orientation。因此该取向是 Markovnikov orientation。

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the regiochemical rule for halohydrin formation: in Markovnikov orientation, the nucleophilic OH ends up on the more substituted alkene carbon while the halogen ends up on the less substituted carbon, due to greater positive character at the more substituted carbon in the bromonium-ion intermediate.
